about: A technical chapter whose paragraph-length headings are capitalised phrases ('Power Supply Unit', 'Signal Path', 'Gain Stage', 'Output Stage') repeated through the chapter; they are no names.
title: The Valve Amplifier
author: Ada Pell

chapters.title: Repair
paragraphs: Iolanthe unpacked the amplifier on the workbench. She had waited three weeks for the parts.
Power Supply Unit
The power supply unit came first. Iolanthe checked the fuse and the mains lead before she touched anything else.
Signal Path
The signal path ran from the input jack to the first valve. Iolanthe traced it with a pencil and marked each joint.
Gain Stage
The gain stage was the part she trusted least. She measured it twice and wrote the numbers in the margin.
Output Stage
The output stage drove the speakers and ran hot. Iolanthe fitted a heat sink and tested it with a dummy load.
Iolanthe switched the amplifier on. She watched the valves glow and waited for the hum to settle.
Power Supply Unit
Back at the power supply unit she found a loose lead. She tightened it and the hum dropped by half.
Signal Path
Along the signal path a cheap capacitor had begun to leak. Iolanthe replaced it and logged the date.
Gain Stage
The gain stage needed a small adjustment. Iolanthe turned the trimmer a quarter turn and listened.
Output Stage
The output stage was sound. She cleaned the contacts and fixed the cover back in place.
Iolanthe played a record to test the whole chain. The first notes came out clean and warm.
She sat back and let the music run. After an hour Iolanthe wrote a short report for the owner.
In the district everyone knew Iolanthe, and nobody had a bad word for Iolanthe.
Years afterwards people still asked about Iolanthe, though few could say why.
